description: A round bell that carries the number of unread notifications; it rattles as the count goes up, the clapper lags behind and the badge digits roll like an odometer.
interactionNotes: It is a button, but its personality comes from the data, not from the click: every time `count` goes up the bell swings around its top hinge, the clapper lags behind on its own spring and the digits roll in the direction of the change. At `max` the badge becomes "+" and at zero it fades out completely. The click itself is normal button behavior (focus, hover, press) and `onClick` is free.

props.count: Number of unread notifications. Every increase rattles the bell; a decrease or staying the same has no rattle.
props.max: From this number up the badge shows "99+" and the digits do not roll.
props.variant: `count` shows the number, `dot` shows just a dot — for when the count does not matter.
props.size: Button diameter in pixels; the bell, badge and badge font are all scaled from it.
props.color: Badge color; the same five default system colors.
props.disabled: Dimmed and unresponsive to the pointer.
props.className: Extra class for the button itself.

tips: Pass `count` from your own data source; the bell rattles as soon as the number goes up, so no `ref` or manual method is needed.
The rattle only comes from the count **increasing**. That is deliberate: reading notifications should not shake the bell.
The digits are Persian and sit in fixed-width boxes because `tabular-nums` has no effect on Peyda's Persian numerals; do not swap them by hand.
The badge sits on the `inline-end` side — in Persian that means the top-left corner. If the `dir` prop on the parent changes, it mirrors itself.
The remaining `<button>` props (such as `onClick` and `aria-label`) go straight to the button; for a custom label, replace the default screen-reader text with `aria-label`.
With `prefers-reduced-motion` the rattle and rolling are removed: the badge appears and the digits jump in place, but the counting logic is untouched.
